URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/jobs-report-october-2026.html
Outlet: CNBC, published Fri Nov 6 2026 8:31 AM EST, updated 11:06 AM EST. By Jeff Cox
Jobs report October 2026: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs

Nonfarm payrolls: 165,000 (vs. forecast of 59,000)
Unemployment rate: 4.1% (vs. forecast of 4.2%)
U-6 unemployment measure: 7.9% (up 0.3 percentage point)
Average hourly earnings: +0.4% monthly, +3.1% annually (vs. forecasts of +0.3% and +2.9%)
Average workweek: 34.4 hours (unchanged)
Civilian labor force increase: 421,000; household employment gain: 463,000
Average unemployment duration: 27.1 weeks (up 2.3 weeks); long-term unemployed (27+ weeks): 1.96 million
Revisions: August revised up to 186,000 (+53,000); September revised up to 60,000 (+31,000)
Sectors: professional and business services +70,000; healthcare +42,000; transportation and warehousing +25,000; manufacturing +19,000

Dan North, Allianz Trade North America: "You have to look pretty hard to find something to dislike in there."
Seema Shah, Principal Asset Management: "Today's jobs report is a strong rebuttal to fears that the economy is heading into a meaningful slowdown."
Heather Long, Navy Federal Credit Union: "The overall picture is a labor market that is on much better footing than a year ago."
